pr_title: List all Debian package versions in `Packages`
pr_body:
Closes #27783

This PR lists all and not only the latest package versions in the `Packages` index.
pr_comments: The test runs too fast and the `ORDER BY created` produces unstable results then.

issue_context.title: Can't get old versions on Debian package registry with apt
issue_context.body:
### Description

When I try to get an older version of a package I get an error. After checking all the packages in the repository, I noticed that only the latest packages of each package group are displayed.

### Gitea Version

1.20.5 built with GNU Make 4.4.1, go1.20.8 : bindata, timetzdata, sqlite, sqlite_unlock_notify

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

Yes

### Log Gist

_No response_

### Screenshots

![image](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/33422161/91d47d5e-7969-4ac8-9631-3828349a5faf)
![image](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/33422161/68b7dfaf-a2d5-4220-9fd8-171e640f267d)
![image](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/33422161/171e41bc-5b5c-49fa-ad22-c44f3e6a43f1)


### Git Version

2.40.1, Wire Protocol Version 2 Enabled

### Operating System

Ubuntu 20.04

### How are you running Gitea?

Docker version on Docker Hub with latest tag

### Database

PostgreSQL
comments: That's by design at the moment. Usually the debian package index contains only the latest available version and only that version is installable with apt.

> That's by design at the moment. Usually the debian package index contains only the latest available version and only that version is installable with apt.

Is it currently necessary to create components for specific versions?
That would be a workaround. I just used the latest package version then because the "big" repositories do the same. But we can list all package versions.

> That would be a workaround. I just used the latest package version then because the "big" repositories do the same. But we can list all package versions.

Yes, I understand. It would be convenient for the component to select all versions or only the latest one. For example, for the "main" component have only the latest version, and for "dev" have all versions
I will change it to list all versions. The Docker repository for example does that too https://download.docker.com/linux/debian/dists/bookworm/stable/binary-amd64/Packages .

> I will change it to list all versions. The Docker repository for example does that too https://download.docker.com/linux/debian/dists/bookworm/stable/binary-amd64/Packages .

Thanks

review_comments:
Is that the correct sorting?
Do we want the sorting
```go
A (yesterday)
A (today)
B (yesterday)
B (today)
```
or do we want
```go
A (today)
B (today)
A (yesterday)
B (yesterday)
```
?

In theory we don't need an order here at all because that file is consumed by the apt client which populates its database with the entries.
The sorting is just for readability if a human has a look at the index.
Looks like this condition has disappeared?
Yes, that's correct. This condition was used to select the latest version.
